correctedState: Confirmed, and broader than filed. `parseMemoryImportPath` (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:49-64) gates on `line.trim().startsWith('@')`, so an `@path` anywhere but the start of a trimmed line is never an import. Executed against the shipped code, all three of the page's own examples resolve to null and inline nothing: `See @README for project overview and @package.json ...`, `- git workflow @docs/git-instructions.md`, and `- @~/.claude/my-project-instructions.md`. The claim's parenthetical that a whole-line `@path` works is only true for the MEMORY.md family and rules files, which native-sources.ts routes through `memoryFileRecords` (:691, :909, :978, :1027, :1092) and its import walker (:427-429). For the files the doc sentence is about — AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / CLAUDE.local.md (PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES, native-sources.ts:82) — `fileRecord('instruction', …)` (:988, :1082, :1089) creates no imported records, and base-agent.ts:966-974 emits the layer body verbatim (the import-stripping filter at :1005 runs only over `runtime.view.memory`), so NO import is expanded there at all and the `@…` line reaches the model as literal text. Exception: on the Claude backend, claude-agent.ts:305 delegates CLAUDE.md loading to the Agent SDK via `settingSources: ['user','project','local']`, so Claude's own import semantics apply there; that backend is off by default. A fix must (a) scan line interiors for `@path` tokens outside code spans and fenced blocks, allowing multiple per line, and (b) run instruction files through the same import walker as memory files.
